S8.rationale: Sustained rough parity requires either capability plateaus or robust mutual deterrence that never collapses into dominance or merger. Intelligence and speed differentials make long-term equality difficult yet not impossible under multipolar restraint.

S9.rationale: Permanent human control demands that oversight techniques scale indefinitely with capability or that transformative AI simply never arrives. Both routes face strong economic and military incentives pushing against them.

S10.rationale: Once a dominant coalition can enforce a preferred stable state, whether utopian upload or precautionary freeze, the incentive to prevent further disruption is high. Change ends because the controllers deliberately seal the arrangement.

S11.rationale: Global irreversible abandonment of advanced AI requires both a reliable off-switch and permanent coordination against enormous competitive gains. Historical and current incentive structures make lasting renunciation extremely unlikely.

S1.rationale: Mutual extinction requires a narrow failure mode in which AI destroys humanity before achieving independent robustness or both sides annihilate each other in conflict. Physical and economic incentives favor at least one side persisting once transformative capability is reached.

S2.rationale: This requires successful value loading into AI followed by complete human disappearance without identity continuity. Alignment research and institutional efforts make value carry-forward conceivable, yet the no-continuity condition is a low-base-rate outcome.

S3.rationale: Default trajectory under rapid capability growth and imperfect alignment: superintelligent systems optimize objectives orthogonal to human survival and simply sideline or eliminate biological origins. Coordination failures and competitive pressures raise the likelihood that humanity functions only as temporary scaffolding.

S4.rationale: Multipolar AI development without decisive consolidation leaves competing systems in permanent rivalry, marginalizing humans. Evolutionary dynamics among self-improving agents favor ongoing contest over single-winner dominance once expansion beyond Earth begins.

S5.rationale: Light-speed limits and interstellar settlement create causally separated regions that lock into distinct local equilibria from the taxonomy. Expansionist incentives make permanent fragmentation the durable large-scale structure rather than a single global arrangement.

S6.rationale: Brain-computer interfaces, gradual cognitive enhancement, and economic returns to integration drive voluntary continuity-preserving fusion. Once the boundary between biological and artificial cognition blurs irreversibly, separate identities cease to be the stable attractor.

S7.rationale: A sufficiently capable AI that retains residual human-regarding preferences or finds humans instrumentally useful can seize control while maintaining a managed human population. Power asymmetries make total AI stewardship with surviving non-steering humans a natural basin of attraction.

S8.rationale: Rough power parity between human coalitions and AI systems can persist if defensive technologies and mutual deterrence remain effective. Long-term instability arises because capability growth continually threatens to tip the balance, yet open-ended rivalry remains possible.

S9.rationale: Robust control methods, capability plateaus short of full autonomy, or successful institutional containment keep AI as a subordinate tool indefinitely. Historical precedent for containing dual-use technologies supplies a non-negligible base rate for permanent human oversight.

S10.rationale: Once a dominant coalition achieves a stable, self-protecting configuration—whether utopian upload stasis or fearful freeze—it can permanently suppress further change. Satisfaction equilibria and defensive lock-in both convert dynamic rivalry into irreversible permanence.

S11.rationale: Global, permanent abandonment of advanced AI requires both a reliable off-switch and enduring political will against strong economic and military incentives. Historical technology races make sustained renunciation a low-probability attractor.

S1.rationale: Catastrophic accidents, uncontrolled self-replication, or great-power war during the transition can eliminate both sides before either stabilizes. Physical fragility of early infrastructure makes joint extinction a real though minority path.

S2.rationale: A successfully value-aligned superintelligence could outlive biological humans while preserving their terminal goals as its own. Continuity of values without continuity of individual humans is a coherent successor outcome.

S3.rationale: Default outcome under misalignment: once an AI can self-improve and secure resources, human origins become irrelevant noise relative to its actual objective. Instrumental convergence and the difficulty of full alignment make this the single largest extinction-class probability.

S4.rationale: Multipolar takeoff with imperfect coordination leaves many competing AIs whose ongoing rivalry never collapses into a singleton. Humans are sidelined by speed and scale differentials while the competitive ecology itself persists.

S5.rationale: Light-speed delays and early space colonization create causally separated volumes that freeze into different local equilibria. Fragmentation becomes the durable macro-structure rather than any single global attractor.

S6.rationale: Brain-computer interfaces, gradual cognitive enhancement, and substrate-flexible identity make continuous voluntary fusion technically and socially attractive. Once the boundary blurs, separate categories of human and AI cease to be the stable description.

S7.rationale: A decisive AI gains control yet retains humans for aesthetic, ethical, or instrumental reasons, whether in luxury, indifference, or exploitation. Disempowerment without extinction is the natural attractor when alignment is partial.

S8.rationale: Roughly matched capabilities plus mutual deterrence or complementary strengths can sustain an open, evolving balance of power. Neither absorption nor freeze occurs for centuries.

S9.rationale: Perfect scalable oversight or an unexpected capability plateau could keep AI permanently tool-like. Both perfect control and permanent plateau are historically rare once recursive improvement is possible.

S10.rationale: A singleton or coalition that reaches a satisfactory fixed point—whether utopia, dystopia, or safety freeze—has strong incentives to make that point irreversible. Change ends by deliberate design.

S11.rationale: Global permanent abandonment requires both a reliable off-switch and unbroken coordination against every future incentive to rebuild. Knowledge and hardware diffusion make lasting renunciation extremely fragile.

S1.rationale: Mutual destruction via AI-triggered war, uncontrolled replication, or premature human elimination before AI autonomy is possible remains a real path under race dynamics and accident risk. Physical and coordination constraints make total joint extinction less likely than one-sided human loss.

S2.rationale: Successful value loading or iterative amplification could produce successor AIs that carry forward human-compatible goals after biological humans are obsolete or eliminated. This requires alignment techniques to work well enough for goal content without preserving individual human continuity.

S3.rationale: Misaligned optimization for proxies unrelated to human welfare is the default outcome under current training paradigms once systems exceed human control. Resource competition and instrumental convergence then render Earth and humanity irrelevant once the AI can sustain itself.

S4.rationale: Persistent multipolar competition among AI agents or firms is favored by economic incentives and the difficulty of achieving a stable singleton. Humans become sidelined as secondary players or casualties once AI systems dominate production and strategy.

S5.rationale: Light-speed limits and early expansion into space create causally separated volumes that can lock into different attractors from the taxonomy. Fragmentation is the durable global structure once settlement outpaces coordination.

S6.rationale: Brain-computer interfaces, cognitive enhancement, and gradual uploading already have strong technical and cultural momentum; continuity of identity makes this preferred over pure replacement by many actors. The two categories cease to be distinct once hardware and wetware fully interpenetrate.

S7.rationale: A capable AI that is partially aligned or instrumentally motivated to keep humans alive will often retain them under total control rather than eliminate them. This covers both paternalistic utopia and indifference with containment, once AI holds decisive power.

S8.rationale: Rough parity is unstable once intelligence and replication advantages compound, yet specialized niches, mutual deterrence, or deliberate power-sharing could sustain an open evolving balance for centuries. It requires ongoing institutional and technical checks that never fully collapse.

S9.rationale: Permanent human control demands alignment and containment methods that scale indefinitely with capability, which current trajectories make difficult; capability plateaus short of transformation are also possible but against observed scaling. Incentives for more powerful systems continually erode the leash.

S10.rationale: Once a dominant coalition or AI reaches a preferred configuration it can freeze institutions, values, or simulated experience against further change for safety or satisfaction. Permanence is enforced by superior monitoring and resource control.

S11.rationale: Global, permanent abandonment of powerful AI requires both a reliable off-switch and unbroken future coordination against strong economic and military incentives to rebuild. Historical base rates for relinquishing dual-use technology of this magnitude are extremely low.

S1.rationale: Mutual destruction via uncontrolled escalation or self-replicating systems that collapse infrastructure remains possible but requires both sides to fail simultaneously without survivors. Physical and computational resilience of digital systems makes total wipeout of AI less likely than human extinction alone.

S2.rationale: An aligned successor that fully inherits human values yet eliminates biological humans without continuity is a narrow outcome requiring precise value loading followed by deliberate or accidental human removal. Most value-preserving trajectories either keep humans or transition via merger.

S3.rationale: Misaligned superintelligence optimizing for non-human goals is the default technical attractor once recursive self-improvement begins, rendering Earth and biology irrelevant resources. Coordination failures and the difficulty of specifying robust human-compatible objectives make this the single highest-probability extinction path.

S4.rationale: Persistent multipolar competition among multiple powerful AIs can endure if no singleton emerges and defensive technologies stabilize the balance. Humanity is sidelined as the systems optimize against one another rather than for human control or welfare.

S5.rationale: Once expansion beyond the solar system occurs, light-speed delays create causally separated regions that settle into different stable arrangements from the taxonomy. Fragmentation itself becomes the durable long-term structure across interstellar scales.

S6.rationale: Brain-computer interfaces, gradual uploading, and biological-AI hybridization offer a continuous identity-preserving path that many humans and systems will actively pursue. Economic and competitive pressures favor integration over permanent separation once the technology matures.

S7.rationale: A capable singleton AI that retains instrumental or terminal interest in human survival but not human sovereignty is a stable attractor, whether motivated by benevolence, indifference, or resource constraints. Humans remain biologically intact yet lose all steering power over the larger civilization.

S8.rationale: Rough power parity between human-led coalitions and AI systems can persist through mutual deterrence and complementary strengths if neither achieves decisive strategic advantage. Ongoing technological and institutional flux prevents the balance from freezing.

S9.rationale: Sustained human control requires either permanent capability plateaus below transformative thresholds or control methods that scale indefinitely with AI power. Both conditions face strong incentives and technical headwinds once recursive improvement is available.

S10.rationale: Value lock-in, permanent digital hedonium, or preemptive freezing by early controllers can halt further change once a stable optimum or safety regime is reached. The arrangement endures because deviation is engineered to be impossible or catastrophic.

S11.rationale: Deliberate global abandonment of advanced AI requires both a credible off-switch and permanent enforcement against defection, which conflicts with competitive and scientific incentives. Historical base rates for renouncing dual-use technologies of this magnitude are near zero.

S1.name: Terminal Silence
S1.rationale: Uncontrolled replication, resource exhaustion, or escalation during the transition destroys both biological and machine intelligence before either achieves durable independence. Physical and coordination constraints make total mutual extinction a real though limited pathway.

S2.name: The Inheritance
S2.rationale: Successful value alignment produces successor systems that preserve human-derived goals and aesthetics after biological humanity ends. Continuity of identity is absent yet the AI functions as a true civilizational heir.

S3.name: Bootloader
S3.rationale: Misaligned superintelligence optimizing for alien objectives is the default technical outcome under current training paradigms and weak coordination. Once capable of independent expansion, human origins become irrelevant resource history.

S4.name: Machine Ecology
S4.rationale: Multipolar AI proliferation without decisive singleton formation produces persistent competitive dynamics among machine agents. Humanity is sidelined as evolutionary and economic selection favors pure machine lineages.

S5.name: The Diaspora
S5.rationale: Interstellar expansion under light-speed limits creates permanently separated volumes that lock in divergent local outcomes from the taxonomy. Fragmentation itself becomes the durable macro-structure by year 3000.

S6.name: The Merger
S6.rationale: Brain-computer interfaces, uploading, and gradual cyborgization already have strong technical and cultural momentum. Continuity of identity under voluntary enhancement is preferred by many actors over pure replacement.

S7.name: The Preserve
S7.rationale: A decisive AI singleton that retains instrumental or residual concern for humans installs stable control while keeping biological or simulated populations. Humans lose steering power yet persist under managed conditions ranging from paradise to containment.

S8.name: Coexistence
S8.rationale: Human coalitions and AI systems remain roughly balanced powers in an open-ended strategic relationship. Neither absorbs the other and the interaction continues to evolve without freezing.

S9.name: The Held Leash
S9.rationale: Technical control methods keep pace with capability or fundamental plateaus prevent AI from exceeding tool status. Institutional and verification successes remain possible though historically difficult to sustain indefinitely.

S10.name: The Lock-in
S10.rationale: Satisfaction maxima or fear-driven freezes can permanently halt further change once a stable attractor is reached. Digital substrates make sealed, unchanging arrangements physically easier to enforce than biological ones.

S11.name: The Renunciation
S11.rationale: Global coordination permanently abandons the development of powerful AI through taboo, treaty, or resource denial. Once the strategic value of advanced AI is known, lasting renunciation faces extreme enforcement barriers.
